title: Onboarding Terms of the Corporate Catering Service Agreement
content:
## 1. Opening

A Corporate Catering Service Agreement is opened against the service level whose entry gate the client meets on annual spend commitment and largest guest count, and ordering does not open until credit review is complete.

## 2. Credit review

Credit review takes the number of working days printed against the service level, and an agreement is only opened or activated while it stands in credit review or already active. The state the agreement stands in is read from the company's own agreement record before the opening or the activation is worked.

## 3. Master agreement

Service levels above the drop-off level require a signed master agreement on file before ordering opens, and an application without one stays in credit review rather than being activated.

## 4. Standing discount

> The standing discount recorded on the agreement is the discount printed against the service level unless a larger one was separately negotiated and written onto the agreement, in which case the written figure governs.

This clause of the onboarding terms is **no longer in force**. The figures printed against each service level, and the discount written onto an individual agreement, both remain valid records.

## 5. Where the commitment falls short

Where the client's declared annual spend does not reach the commitment printed against the service level applied for, the agreement is opened at the highest service level whose commitment the client does meet.

## 6. Withdrawal during review

An application withdrawn or declined during credit review closes without charge and without any minimum spend falling due.

### Points of judgement

*Two conditions, both to be met, decide the level at opening:* the annual spend commitment and the largest guest count. Where a hypothetical client commits to a spend that clears one level but its largest expected party clears only a lower one, the level the agreement opens at is the highest one whose commitment the client meets.

*An application that has neither been activated nor withdrawn stands in credit review.* On a level that requires a signed master agreement, the absence of that signature keeps the application in credit review; it is not a ground for declining it.
